strengths.item: The paper evaluates FFCA-Net on three stereo datasets using standard rate-distortion metrics including bpp, PSNR, MS-SSIM, BD-rate, and BD-PSNR.
It compares against a reasonably broad set of single-image, joint stereo, and distributed/asymmetric stereo compression baselines.
The method is accompanied by ablations for major components, including stereo patch matching, hourglass-based sparse stereo refinement, and Fast Feature Fusion.
The appendix provides useful implementation details such as dataset splits, bitrate operating points, training settings, and component-level speed/parameter comparisons.

weaknesses.item: Baseline comparisons are only partially controlled: some results are taken from original papers, not all baselines are evaluated on all datasets, and several baselines appear to be evaluated using published parameters rather than uniformly retrained or fine-tuned.

The decoding latency and FLOPs claims are under-supported because the timing protocol lacks important details such as batch size, warm-up, precision, software versions, CPU/GPU timing methodology, and whether entropy decoding or I/O is included.

The ablations do not fully isolate all claimed contributions. In particular, stereo patch matching is not independently ablated from HSSR, and FFF is mainly a speed component but the main ablation table does not report end-to-end latency for the W/O FFF variant.
The acceleration ablations compare modules with substantially different parameter counts and do not clearly preserve matched quality or capacity, making causal attribution of speed gains weaker.
The statistical reporting is limited: there are no confidence intervals, repeated-run variance, per-image dispersion, significance tests, or detailed BD-rate computation procedures.

The distributed compression formulation and bitrate accounting are under-specified, especially regarding whether side information is assumed to be freely available at the decoder and whether bpp is measured per main image, per stereo pair, or with any side-information costs included.

dimension_review.evidence_summary: The paper provides a plausible technical framework and reports strong rate-distortion and speed results across KITTI-stereo, Cityscapes, and InStereo2K. It includes many standard baselines and ablations, and the appendix adds dataset split and training details. However, the Q&A identified several methodological gaps: baseline evaluation is not fully uniform, latency comparisons lack a rigorous timing protocol, ablations are entangled or only component-level, statistical uncertainty is not reported, and the assumptions behind decoder-side side information and rate accounting are not clearly specified.
dimension_review.rationale: The evidence supports that FFCA-Net may be an effective stereo compression method, and the experiments are more substantial than a minimal empirical validation. However, the central claims of superior rate-distortion performance and faster decoding are weakened by fairness and accounting ambiguities, incomplete causal ablations, and lack of statistical rigor. These issues are important for soundness because compression performance is highly sensitive to bitrate definitions, baseline training/evaluation protocol, RD interpolation details, and runtime measurement methodology. Therefore, the soundness is fair rather than good or excellent.
